newsitem.title: USA: Mild weather, more supply pound NYMEX electricity.
newsitem.headline: Mild weather, more supply pound NYMEX electricity.

text.p: Forecasts of mild spring temperatures and rising generation in the West pounded the NYMEX electricity complex lower Tuesday, extending Monday's dramatic reversal from its recent run-up.
"There's no reason to be bullish right now...It's going to be soft for the next couple of days," said a West Coast futures trader.

Weaker natural gas futures and another price cut from Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) on its next-day products also contributed to a slump in futures prices for a second day, market sources said.
NYMEX July Henry Hub natgas futures settled down 0.7 cent at $2.103 per million British thermal units after finding support at $2.080.
BPA today lowered its peak, firm power for next-day delivery by $4.00 to $15.00-16.00 after slashing prices by $11.00-12.00 Monday.
In just two sessions, July California-Oregon Border (COB) futures lost $6.83 a megawatt hour (MWh) or 27.9 percent of their value, while the July Palo Verde (PV) contract fell $5.80 or 17.4 percent.
July COB settled today down $3.49 at $17.61 after hitting a low of $17.25. August COB finished down $2.84 at $21.22. Deferred COB ended 15 cents to $1.94 lower.
July PV settled down $2.91 at $27.66 after posting a session low of $27.20. August PV finished down $2.42 at $29.98. Deferred PV ended 80 cents to $1.64 lower.

Spot physical power prices in the West finished sharply lower again. Firm, peak deliveries for Wednesday at COB dropped $6.00 to $13.00-15.00, while those at PV tumbled more than $10.00 to $27.00-29.00.

Two nuclear power units, the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 and 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3, are in the process of returning to full output following outages, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico was expected to restart at midnight Tuesday, slightly behind its original schedule.
But a 550 MW unit at the Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming will shut Wednesday and stay down until Sunday for planned maintenance, industry sources said.
Market players agree the drop in power futures to continue, but the severity of the losses should lessen.
"We'll see come off again tomorrow, but it'll be a minor turn," said a West Coast electricity dealer.

Temperatures in the West were called to average near to slightly above normal into early next week with above normal precipitation in the eastern sections of the Northwest and northern areas of the Southwest.
